title: The Arcadia Formation: infrastructure, governance, land, and the station

history.change: Initial structured reporter report compiled from the receipted Arcadia field-autopsy case and its candidate-only evidence trails.

cells.record_target: Executed right-of-way, easement, parking, and local land-contribution instruments.
Executed betterment agreement, cost-share approvals, and the officials or boards authorizing each local scope addition.
Executed station betterment and funding agreements with itemized scope, amount, payer, approval date, and amendment history.
A complete denominator of downtown applications, approvals, denials, density concessions, public-land dispositions, and completed or failed delivery.
Original enabling resolution or petition, engineer's report, assessment roll, renewal record, bylaws, agendas, support authorizations, votes, recusals, and city oversight file.
Any DAIA agenda, support, authorization, recusal, or city communication specific to the project; none is established in the opened case.
Recorder deed images and grantor-grantee chain before 2016, project option or purchase agreements, applicant-control records, and any project-specific DAIA or city communication.
The DAIA support letter and authorization record, complete applicant-control and beneficial-ownership chain, meeting calendars, votes or recusals, and the city's project decision file.
Final bid tab, award, funding sources, scope changes, property-owner contributions, maintenance agreements, and any DAIA support or design role.

controls.title: Comparable corridors show public planning and parcel assembly without shared Arcadia actors
Policy, land economics, anticipation, and lawful growth coalitions are ordinary mechanisms
Documented cultural market mechanisms are not city policy or coordination evidence

workplan.title: Recover the deed chain before interpreting ownership concentration

Reconcile the station cost share and every local betterment
Resolve who authorized project-specific advocacy and participation
Inventory public land, easements, and disposition decisions

Build same-line and different-corridor controls before interpreting convergence
